Fifa news … Kozo Tashima said he hasn’t talked yet with fellow Fifa presidential race challenfer Philippe Diallo, but he’s willing to work with the Frenchman to defeat Gianni Infantino’s bid for a controversial fourth term.
Tashima and Diallo are two long-shot candidates to replace Infantino in an election set for 18 March. So there’s still plenty time to sway Fifa’s 211 member federations.
“We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he’s a great person to team up with,” Tashima said in comments translated from Japanese. “I’m not looking at Diallo as opposition. I just want to change Fifa. Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management. I do trust him. At this point I’m not think about withdrawing.”
Tashima, who repeated the words “integrity, fairness, trust and transparency” when asked why he decided to stand, is going against the endorsement of the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), which last month pledged support for Infantino — with Infantino on hand at the meeting in Tokyo.
“I just don’t only want to be the Fifa president, my intention was to make Fifa better,” Tashima added. “Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organisation.
“I believe the worst outcome would be for him (Infantino) to remain in office without an election,” he said. “I believe this is a test of whether Fifa truly has the capacity for self-reform. “He’s done a lot of things to make us doubt his integrity,” Tashima said, adding that income from the World Cup – or anywhere else – “is not an Infantino asset. It belongs to Fifa.”
In a three-candidate election, votes from two-thirds of the eligible members are needed to win in the first round. For the second round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and a simple majority will win. In a two-candidate race, Infantino would need votes from 106 of the 211 member federations to win re-election.
Drone footage of Pochettino’s first training session posted on YouTube
Footage from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager has appeared online after being captured by a drone operator. A 12-minute video of the session was posted on to YouTube by an account called CC OVERVIEW after being captured at United’s Carrington training ground. Pochettino and his United players can be seen in the video, with the squad having been divided into three groups.
On the post, the drone operator wrote: “For the people asking about legality. It is unrestricted airspace, meaning anyone can fly over it. The drone remained in line of sight at all times, it didn’t fly over anyone or even near anyone so was a perfectly legal flight going by the CAA rules that regulates drone usage.
“The drone is correctly labelled, and I hold all the relevant licences, public liability and insurance required. As for leaking team news/tactics, it was half an hour into the manager’s first training session, there are many media there so certainly won’t be the only footage of training released.”
Manchester United have declined to comment.
Pochettino was taking his first training session after being appointed as United’s new head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked with the club in the relegation zone during this international window. Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday, having taken charge of the United States for the final time in their 2-0 win over Haiti, which finished in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time. His first match in charge will be a visit to old rivals Liverpool on Sunday afternoon. Press Association
Preamble
Thanks international football, the FA Cup and the Manchester United brains trust, that was fun. We’ll see you again soon. Now it’s time to lock in on pure club action for the foreseeable.
There are seven Premier League fixtures on Saturday, including five in the traditional 3pm slot, two more on Sunday and then Monday night football too. The Championship is also back with 11 fixtures on Saturday and a midday Lancashire derby on Sunday, completing a full slate of EFL after League One and League Two gamely held the fort for the past two weeks – manna from heaven.
Two top-flight clubs come into this post-Nations League bloc with a new man in the dugout. The aforementioned United and fellow basement dwellers Crystal Palace. Thomas Frank’s Eagles go to Coventry (a team managed by Frank Lampard), which looks like both a tricky test and a presentable opportunity for the new man in charge at Palace. Mauricio Pochettino gets a nice easy one first up, away at Liverpool.
Pochettino has already had a taste of the scrutiny that being in charge at Old Trafford brings, with part of his first training session captured by a drone enthusiast and shared on YouTube. Safe to say, people weren’t going to those lengths to see how Tim Ream’s ball progression drills went in USMNT camp.
If we get anymore high-profile drone action or other newsworthy football items this blog will be across it, plus we’ll have updates from the various press conferences taking place today. Do follow along and you can get in touch via the email link at the top of the page.
